question: How many people will Polish prosecutors have publicly named as charged in the Zondacrypto investigation as of October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class anchor: large Polish prosecutorial fraud/organized-crime probes at ~5 months in typically have a handful of publicly named podejrzani, accumulating in clustered sweeps rather than steadily. The concrete base here is firm: the official gov.pl kalendarium names exactly 5 charged individuals (Radoslaw P.; R.Z., J.W., A.P.; Roman Z.), and CoinDesk/The Block called Roman Z. the 'fifth suspect' on 7-8 Sep. The key update is negative: nothing new has been announced in the 14 days since 7 Sep, so the burst cadence implied by the background has not continued; only ~9 days remain to 1 Oct. Upward mass comes from three channels: another sweep in an investigation prosecutors call a 'breakthrough' with new cooperating witnesses (charges here arrive in batches of 1-3), official confirmation of Kral's status (PK spokesperson explicitly declined to disclose it on 7 Sep), and a resolver counting Marian W. 'Maniek', charged in the merged Suszek disappearance thread and included in prawo.pl's list of six. Counterargument to going high: the immunity-protected political thread (Ziobro, Moskal, Czarnek) cannot produce charges within 9 days, and the last two weeks of prosecutorial output were detention appeals and creditor notices, not new suspects. No human market prices this (none on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers), so no external anchor. Median lands just under 6: most likely 5 or 6.

Upside runs through three partly-overlapping channels: a fresh sweep (~30%, batch 1-3), PK formally confirming Kral (~8%, since PK is deliberately withholding his status while he cooperates), and a resolver counting Marian W. from the merged Suszek thread (~14%, though his charges pre-date the 17.04.2026 opening). calls.reconciliation: All three runs fetched the same gov.pl kalendarium and returned an identical set of charge entries totalling five natural persons - that factual point is settled and is the floor. Two ambiguity channels were disputed. (a) Kral: Run 2 treated prok. Piotr Kosmaty's rp.pl statement 'ma status podejrzanego' as public confirmation; Runs 1 and 3 both place Kosmaty as an external prosecutor-commentator inferring from media, and both quote PK spokesperson Anna Adamiak on 07.09 explicitly declining to reveal his status 'zgodnie z decyzja prokuratora'. The criterion requires confirmation by a prosecutorial body acting in this case, so I resolve against counting Kral, and note the question's own background agrees ('prosecutors had not formally confirmed this publicly'). (b) Marian W.: Run 2 dates his charges to end-2025 in the fuel-invoice/deprivation-of-liberty case, Run 3 calls them separate proceedings, Run 1 notes they originate in the Suszek probe merged into this one on 30.07.2026. The dossiers cannot settle whether a resolver counts a charge presented before this investigation opened but inside a proceeding later merged with it; I let that carry its uncertainty as ~14% mass rather than picking a side, which is what pushes meaningful weight onto 6. The remaining dispute is pure judgment - the 9-day arrival rate. The runs weighted the 27.08-07.09 burst rate heavily; I weight the 14-day lull, the absence of any scheduled prosecutorial action found by all three runs, the extension to January 2027 removing deadline pressure, and immunity blocking the political thread, giving ~30% for at least one further charged person. Net: I land below every member (median 5.4 vs their 5.8-6.2) because the reconciled reading of both ambiguity channels is strict and the cadence evidence is a stop, not a pause. Reference class is carried forward from Run 3 (comparable Polish mega-probes at ~5 months, ~6 named), which I agree with; my median sits below it because the case-specific lull and the strict counting basis dominate the class prior. Market check: none found on any venue, consistent across the harness search and all three runs; I retrieved nothing myself this run.
